pr.author: azhogin

classification.name: ElaborateDrops
evidence: use crate::elaborate_drop::{DropElaborator, DropFlagMode, DropStyle, Unwind, elaborate_drop};

The PR fixes an async-drop ICE by changing `DropCtxt::build_drop` to read block data through `MirPatch::block` instead of indexing the original body directly. That drop elaboration engine belongs to the concrete `ElaborateDrops` MIR pass; the `patch.rs` change is a shared helper extraction, not a pass.

analysis.originalLogic: During async-drop elaboration in the `ElaborateDrops` pass, `DropCtxt::build_drop` decides whether to build an async drop for the current block by inspecting that block's `is_cleanup` flag. The check is guarded by `async_drop` being enabled, the body being a coroutine, async drops being allowed, and the dropped type needing an async drop. The block lookup must resolve `bb` against the correct block namespace because the pass may already have inserted new blocks through `MirPatch`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation indexed the original MIR body directly when reading `is_cleanup`: `!self.elaborator.body()[bb].is_cleanup`. This assumes every `BasicBlock` index `bb` is within the original `body.basic_blocks`, but `bb` may instead be an index for a newly added block in `MirPatch` (`bb.index() >= body.basic_blocks.len()`). The correction routes the lookup through a universal getter: `!self.elaborator.patch_ref().block(self.elaborator.body(), bb).is_cleanup`, where `block` uses `bb.index().checked_sub(body.basic_blocks.len())`: `Some(new) => &self.new_blocks[new], None => &body[bb]`. The PR description states the problem was "block data access with block id from new added blocks in patch."
analysis.inputDomain: Functions compiled with the `async_drop` feature, in an async/coroutine body, where drop elaboration is performed on a partially dropped aggregate (e.g. a tuple) and the elaboration path queries `is_cleanup` for a block that belongs to `MirPatch`'s newly added blocks rather than the original body.
analysis.summary: Bug fix in the `ElaborateDrops` MIR pass: async-drop elaboration read `is_cleanup` from the original body using a block id that could refer to a new block added by `MirPatch`, causing an ICE on partly dropped tuples. The fix uses a shared `MirPatch::block` getter that resolves both original-body and patched block indices, and reuses it in `terminator_loc` and `source_info_for_location`.
analysis.trigger: Async-drop elaboration reaches `DropCtxt::build_drop` with a `bb` whose index is at or beyond `body.basic_blocks.len()`, i.e. a block newly appended by `MirPatch`. Directly indexing `body[bb]` then accesses the wrong block/out-of-range data instead of the patched block's `is_cleanup`.
preconditions: the dropped type needs an async drop (`drop_ty.needs_async_drop(...)`)
a partly dropped aggregate/tuple causes drop elaboration to query `is_cleanup` on a block id introduced by `MirPatch`
pitfalls: Do not assume all `BasicBlock` indices are original body indices; `MirPatch` appends new blocks after `body.basic_blocks.len()`.
There are two block namespaces: original `body` blocks and `MirPatch::new_blocks`; resolve via `checked_sub(body.basic_blocks.len())`.
The same old/new block lookup pattern existed in `terminator_loc` and `source_info_for_location`; the fix centralizes it in `MirPatch::block` to avoid divergent handling.
Checking `is_cleanup` on the wrong block can silently alter async-drop construction or cause an ICE, so this is not merely a refactor.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `build-pass` UI regression test under `tests/ui/async-await/async-drop/partly-dropped-tuple.rs` for edition 2024 with `#![crate_type = "lib"]`, `#![allow(incomplete_features)]`, and `#![feature(async_drop)]`. The test defines an async fn that creates a tuple of `Vec`s, drops one element (partial move/drop), and returns the other element: `let x = (vec![3], vec![4, 4]); drop(x.1); x.0`. This exercises async-drop elaboration on a partly dropped tuple and should compile after the fix.
